messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alerta: GPU pool 'inference-high' saturating, queue growth detected (qps spike) - see dashboards: https://grafana/redwood/d/serve/queue

Alice Rivera: ack. I'm on it. Paging oncall.

Carlos Gomez: oncall here. Observing 95% utilization, 5m p95 latency 3.2s, 429 throttle rate rising. Which model?

incident-bot: Top hot routes: /v1/generate (gpt-large-8k) 60% of queue, /v1/chat (redwood-chat) 25%. Autoscaler failing to add nodes: scale_events show repeated "scale rejected: quota-limit" for 3 attempts.

Sam Cho: looks like autoscaler hit maxPoolSize (config) on that cluster. Also continuous-batching hit drop: prefix-cache miss rate jumped -> ineffective batching -> higher per-token cost & queue.

Meera Patel: prefix cache TTL was rolled from 30s -> 5s in last rollout at 01:06 UTC (recent infra change). That would cause cache churn. I'm pulling the rollout.

Jenna Li: customer impact: 4 tenant clusters showing 429 spikes, multiple customers seeing failed realtime requests. SLAs impacted for three enterprise customers. We should triage severity -> Sev2.

Alice Rivera: mitigation plan, quick steps: 1) pin autoscaler maxReplicas up, 2) revert prefix-cache-ttl rollback, 3) limit request concurrency via rate-limiter if needed, 4) divert some traffic to lower-capacity model variant. We need someone to execute 1&2 now.

Sam Cho: executing autoscaler patch now. Running:
```
kubectl -n inference patch gpupool inference-high --type merge -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":40}}'
```
Sam Cho: submitted, controller accepted. Provisioning new nodes (request -> cloud provider). ETA ~ 3m.

Meera Patel: rolling back prefix-cache TTL change in config repo and applying to runtime. Patch:
```
./deploy-configs.sh --set prefix_cache.ttl=30s --env prod --target inference-high
```
Meera Patel: applied. Cache warmup expected ~2-4m.

infra-bot: Cloud provider report: 6 new GPU instances requested, 4 allocated, 2 delayed due to capacity in region. Pending queue length for pool increased.

Carlos Gomez: while we wait, throttling customers with high qps on /v1/generate by lowering their weights on the router. Applying routing rule now.

Alice Rivera: please also reduce continuous-batching window from 200ms -> 100ms for hot routes to reduce tail latency. Meera please apply.

Meera Patel: done. Patch:
```
PATCH /config/continuous-batching
{"routes":{"/v1/generate":{"batch_window_ms":100}}}
```
Meera Patel: change active in 30s.

Jenna Li: monitoring shows p50->p95 gap narrowing, throttle rate plateauing. Still seeing 429s for a small percent. Customer success pinged customers and posting status update.

Sam Cho: new nodes ready: 4 of 6 succeeded. Autoscaler still trying to reach requested capacity; controller reports "scale-burst-disabled: pool-safety-check" while we have hot-shard lock. I'm going to force-add 2 warm nodes via infra console.

Sam Cho: forced add done. pool now at 34 GPUs. Queue draining slowly.

Meera Patel: prefix cache miss rate dropped from 78% -> 12% after rollback and warmup. Batching efficiency improved (tokens/second up ~2.3x on hot route).

incident-bot: Metrics snapshot at 1780012375: queue_length=420 -> 90, p95_latency=3.2s -> 1.1s, throttle_rate=12% -> 2.1%.

Alice Rivera: good progress. Next: we need a short-term fix to avoid region capacity causing repeated failures. Options: a) enable cross-region fallback for autoscaler, b) pre-warm reserved nodes for peak windows. Which is quickest?

Carlos Gomez: cross-region fallback is medium effort. Pre-warm reserved nodes is ops heavy but fastest: we can spin up 10 reserved gpus in us-west2 now and route overflow. I'll coordinate with infra.

Jenna Li: I'll update status page: "Degraded performance for realtime generation endpoints. Engineers mitigating; some customers may experience timeouts or throttling. Next update in 20m."

Meera Patel: quick note for postmortem: the rollout that reduced prefix_cache.ttl was gated but not in canary for high-throughput routes; continuous-batching defaults were permissive. Need a rollout gate by qps quartile.

Alice Rivera: agreed. For now, handoff: Carlos will stay and finish capacity ops; Sam will follow up on autoscaler limits; Meera will open rollback PR and a canary plan; Jenna will own customer comms. I'm heading offshift in 10m; handing to oncall-next.

oncall-next: ack handoff. I'll coordinate capacity until stable. Please add incident notes to the tracker: https://jira/redwood/browse/INC-3819

Carlos Gomez: final check: queue < 50, p95 ~0.95s, throttle rate <1%. I'm marking this as mitigated for live traffic, continuing monitoring for 2 hours.

Alice Rivera: +1. Post-incident actions: 1) revert risky rollout gating, 2) adjust autoscaler safety mechanism to allow emergency scaling beyond pool-safety-check with human override, 3) add canarying for prefix-cache/continuous-batching changes, 4) load test warm nodes in us-west2. Assign owners in the Jira.

incident-bot: Incident closed for paging. Severity: Sev2 -> mitigated. Full postmortem required.

Jenna Li: will schedule postmortem and invite infra, runtime, and product.

Meera Patel: logging the exact commits for rollback: commit abc1234ef -> reverted.

Carlos Gomez: customers notified. I'll follow up with finance for potential credits if SLA breach confirmed.

Alice Rivera: thanks team. Good work moving quickly. :clap:
